summary: Risk plan for gpt-copy-v8 identifies the main delivery hazards around OpenRouter isolation, streaming SSE reliability, SQLite/sqlx schema behavior, frontend/backend contract drift, automated tests accidentally depending on provider quota, and completion claims before full verification.

proposals.title: Mock-first provider boundary
proposals.summary: Define a backend OpenRouter client trait or narrow module boundary early so endpoint tests can simulate success, 429, timeout, invalid response, and interrupted stream behavior without external calls.

proposals.title: Contract-first API payloads
proposals.summary: Keep backend request/response DTOs and frontend zod schemas aligned around a small set of JSON shapes for conversations, messages, validation errors, and stream chunks before building broad UI behavior.

proposals.title: Verification gate for completion reports
proposals.summary: Treat formatting, linting, builds, backend tests, frontend component tests, Playwright smoke, and tracked-secret scan as blocking checks before any CodeDungeon report claims COMPLETE.

risks.title: Automated tests could hit real OpenRouter
risks.impact: External calls can leak secrets, consume quota, fail nondeterministically, or violate the project rule forbidding provider calls from automated tests.
risks.mitigation: Inject a mockable OpenRouter client into handlers and assert in tests that mocked responses drive success, 429, timeout, invalid response, and interrupted stream paths.

risks.title: Streaming SSE can desynchronize persisted state
risks.impact: If assistant chunks are persisted too early or not finalized after stream failure, users may see duplicate, partial, or missing assistant messages after reload.
risks.mitigation: Persist the user message before provider streaming, buffer assistant content until completion, mark interrupted streams as structured errors, and add tests for cancellation and provider failure.

risks.title: OpenRouter error handling can crash or expose provider internals
risks.impact: Unhandled 429, timeout, malformed JSON, or network interruption can panic the Axum service or return raw provider errors to the browser.
risks.mitigation: Map provider failures to typed application errors with stable JSON/SSE error payloads and sanitized tracing fields; cover each mapping with mocked backend tests.

risks.title: Frontend may bypass backend for model calls
risks.impact: A direct browser request to OpenRouter would expose OPENROUTER_API_KEY or break local operation because secrets are server-only.
risks.mitigation: Keep all model calls behind backend endpoints, expose only NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL to the frontend, and scan tracked frontend files for OPENROUTER_API_KEY usage before completion.

risks.title: SQLite/sqlx setup may require unavailable offline metadata
risks.impact: Using compile-time sqlx macros without prepared metadata can make worker builds fail in clean environments or CI.
risks.mitigation: Prefer runtime-checked sqlx query APIs for this fixture or include a clear sqlx prepare workflow; verify with cargo check and cargo test from a clean checkout.

risks.title: Next.js 15 and React test stack compatibility
risks.impact: Component tests can become brittle if app-router components, server/client boundaries, Tailwind setup, or testing-library configuration are inconsistent.
risks.mitigation: Keep interactive chat components as explicit client components, isolate API code behind testable hooks/modules, and add focused Vitest component tests before Playwright smoke.

risks.title: CORS and local URL defaults can block the smoke path
risks.impact: The frontend smoke test can fail even when backend logic works if FRONTEND_ORIGIN, BACKEND_HOST, BACKEND_PORT, or NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL defaults disagree.
risks.mitigation: Centralize backend config defaults, document exact run commands, and have Playwright use the same local API base URL expected by the frontend.

risks.title: Generated artifacts may be accidentally tracked
risks.impact: SQLite databases, frontend build outputs, Playwright reports, node_modules, or Rust target files can pollute the PR and obscure review.
risks.mitigation: Keep existing .gitignore coverage, add any missing generated paths before running tools, and check git status before final handoff.

risks.title: Completion may be overstated before review and verification
risks.impact: The final report would violate project rules if it claims COMPLETE without passing verification and receiving approved review status.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit verification results and an APPROVED review state before final CodeDungeon reporting uses COMPLETE; otherwise report remaining blockers.

claims.title: Provider calls stay server-side
claims.summary: OpenRouter access must be implemented only in the Rust backend and configured through OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_MODEL.

claims.title: Secrets remain local
claims.summary: .env remains ignored, .env.example contains placeholders/defaults only, and tracked files must be scanned for OpenRouter keys before completion.

claims.title: Streaming is the highest-complexity path
claims.summary: SSE combines provider IO, persistence ordering, cancellation, frontend incremental rendering, and error handling, so it should receive the most focused tests.

claims.title: No material user ambiguity
claims.summary: The prompt and approved project rules are sufficient for planning; no human gate is needed at this phase.
